key_insight: FCV-PICRN reconstructs flow structures across large unsupervised gaps by combining Fourier features, complex-valued learning, and Navier–Stokes constraints.
engineering_relevance: The approach could improve flow-field estimation when measurements are sparse, noisy, or unavailable in critical wake regions.
method: Fourier features represent oscillatory and multiscale flow structures.
Complex-valued convolutional residual blocks learn coupled amplitude–phase representations.
Navier–Stokes constraints guide reconstruction where supervised velocity data are absent.
evidence_signal: Tests covered Taylor–Green and cylinder-wake flows at Re=100, three severe gap geometries, robustness under up to 20% Gaussian noise, and lower errors than a conventional PINN for 2D Kolmogorov turbulence with 5% Gaussian noise.
watch_item: Generalization to three-dimensional, higher-Reynolds-number flows and computational cost are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Fourier-Feature-Embedded Complex-Valued Physics-Informed Convolutional Residual Networks for Sparse and Gappy Noisy Flow-Field Reconstruction
